summary.text: A 62-year-old male with diabetes mellitus, coronary artery occlusive disease, nonST elevation myocardial infarction, peripheral artery occlusive disease, chronic kidney disease on hemodialysis, hypertension, asthma and subclinical hypothyroidism had chronic osteomyelitis of the right foot and underwent right below-knee amputation four months before presentation. He was admitted to a rehabilitation department for comprehensive prosthetic rehabilitation therapy and complained of neck pain on hospital day 20.

A cervical radiograph showed disc space narrowing without other significant abnormalities, neck pain worsened by HD 27, and MRI could not be performed because of pain, so CT was done. Elevated C-reactive protein raised suspicion of cervical vertebral osteomyelitis, and intravenous vancomycin and a Philadelphia neck brace were started. Nerve conduction studies on HD 41 and evoked potentials were abnormal; from HD 42 he had weakness in all four extremities, tetraparesis and respiratory insufficiency. MRI on HD 44 showed C6-7 changes consistent with osteomyelitis.

After neurosurgical consultation surgery was deemed high-risk, so conservative treatment continued with added moxifloxacin. He had Foley catheterization, escalation to high-flow oxygen and a three-day intensive care stay with continuous renal replacement therapy. Follow-up CT on HD 52 showed progressive C6-7 spondylodiscitis, a soft tissue mass suggestive of phlegmon, probable cord compression and subluxation; neurological function further declined by HD 52. From HD 56 piperacillin/tazobactam was given for six weeks, and active rehabilitation resumed after return to nasal oxygen.

Over one year of rehabilitation including physical therapy, occupational therapy and functional electrical stimulation, the patient improved to AIS D with a neurological level of C6, a motor score of 54 and a sensory score of 73, and had no treatment failure. Table 1 records the AIS grade, motor and sensory scores, SCIM scores and neck pain scale at hospital days and follow-up visits.

ambiguities.issue: The same cervical CT (HD 27) is described as showing disc space destruction in the text and disc space narrowing in the Figure 2a caption.

Text AIS motor scores are not merged with Table 1 motor-score rows because the text does not name the row; sensory scores and AIS grade and level are merged where text and table state the same value at the same time. Compressive myelopathy certainty (abstract confirmed vs text possible) is quarantined as a source conflict.
Text-only CT findings that the Figure 2 captions do not state carry no time (the caption time governs only its own content); findings the captions state keep HD 27/44/52.
Figure pixels are described only in the separate visual submission; the figure rows here keep not_inspected.
The Introduction statement about tetraplegia in published reports and the literature statements about vertebral osteomyelitis were treated as background, not patient facts.
